prerequisites: Good knowledge in college math and physics and in applied math (with a focus on differential and integral calculus in 1,2,3 variables, vector algebra and analysis, complex number and complex exponentials, simple differential equations, Fourier transform)
Good knowledge and ability on circuit theory, above all on AC circuits

learning_outcomes.text: Students must know the properties of electromagnetic fields and the main devices that use them.
Students must be able to correctly evaluate the effects of electromagnetic phenomena on the behavior of ICT (and, more generally, electronic) equipment.
The student will have developed the ability to find and apply standard solutions to the different cases that he may face, and to evaluate their feasibility.
The knowledge acquired will allow the student to subsequently deal with the study and integration of equipment, systems and services that use electromagnetic fields.
These skills will also be useful to those who will not deal directly with these activities, as it will allow future engineers to interact efficiently with the designers of electromagnetic devices.

syllabus_topics: Elementary sources, near and far field
Plane wave, polarization, propagation in material media, plane interfaces
assessment_rules: To pass the exam, it is necessary to obtain at least 5 points in the multiple-choice questions part and at least 8 points in the numerical exercise part, with a final score of 18 or more. The final score is the sum of the results of the two parts, plus 0.15 points, rounded to the closest integer. To obtain "30 cum laude", a final score of at least 32 points is required.
